author: Holquist, Peter
title: Violent Russia, Deadly Marxism? Russia in the Epoch of Violence, 1905-21
publisher: Kritika: Explorations in Russian and Eurasian History 4:3, 627-652
notes: The post-archival re-framing of the argument about revolutionary violence, posted open-access with the journal's permission and read in full here at page level. Holquist maps the field into a school of "circumstances" (Buldakov, Figes: a Russian Sonderweg) and a school of "ideology" (the Black Book, Malia, Pipes: Marxism or the revolutionary tradition as the font), argues that both de-historicise, and proposes the 1905-21 conjuncture inside the European crisis of 1914-24 instead. Also the safest available route to what Buldakov and Figes say, because he quotes them; a position reached only through him is labelled as such wherever this project uses one.
